input: Set up a monthly family budget review dinner

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing who is included (e.g., just adults, or kids too) determines how the meeting is structured, what financial detail is shared, and how formal the conversation needs to be.
Knowing which budget categories or financial topics are on the agenda (spending, savings, debt, investments) shapes what prep work and materials are needed each month.
Whether the dinner is at home or a restaurant, and which day/time of month it happens, affects scheduling, cost, and the practicality of reviewing financial documents.
Knowing what tool or system is used to track the budget (spreadsheet, app, paper) determines how data is pulled together and displayed during the review.
Understanding time limits — how long each session should last — prevents the dinner from feeling like a stressful all-night meeting and helps set a realistic agenda.
The tone (casual and relaxed vs. structured and formal) affects how the agenda is designed, who leads it, and whether it feels like a family ritual or a business meeting.
Defining what a successful review looks like — e.g., decisions made, targets set, everyone feeling heard — determines what outcomes to track and whether the habit is working.

gold.taskTitle: Set up a monthly family budget review dinner
gold.taskDescription: Establish a recurring monthly dinner where the family gathers to review their budget together.

questions.title: Who in the family will attend each dinner?
questions.description: Identify whether this includes only adults/partners, teenagers, or the whole family including young children, as this shapes how financial information is presented and discussed.

questions.title: Which financial topics will each session cover?
questions.description: Clarify which budget areas are reviewed monthly — such as household spending, savings goals, debt repayment, or investments — to define the meeting agenda.

questions.title: Where will the dinner take place each month?
questions.description: Determine whether the budget review dinner happens at home or at a restaurant, and on which recurring day, to lock in a repeatable setting and schedule.

questions.title: What tool do you currently use to track your budget?
questions.description: Identify the existing budgeting system (e.g., spreadsheet, app like YNAB or Mint, paper notebook) so the review process can be built around pulling and displaying data from it.

questions.title: How long should each dinner review session last?
questions.description: Set a target duration for the budget portion of the evening so the agenda can be scoped realistically and the event stays enjoyable rather than draining.

questions.title: Should the tone be casual and relaxed or structured and formal?
questions.description: Understand whether the family prefers a loose, conversational check-in over a meal or a more organised meeting with a set agenda and assigned roles.

questions.title: What would make each monthly review feel successful?
questions.description: Define the desired outcomes — such as agreeing on next month's targets, resolving overspending, or simply keeping everyone informed — to evaluate whether the ritual is working.
